questions.q: Phrase or clause: 'under the tall banyan tree' vs 'when the rain stopped'.
questions.a: First = phrase (no subject-verb). Second = dependent clause (subject 'rain', verb 'stopped', leaning word 'when'). A wrong answer swapping them shows the student tests by length, not structure.

questions.q: 'Because she practised daily' — complete sentence or not?
questions.a: Not — 'because' makes the clause lean on a missing main clause. Complete: 'She won because she practised daily.' A wrong answer accepting it alone shows the dependent-fragment error.

questions.q: How many clauses: 'The sun set, and the birds flew home.'
questions.a: Two independent clauses joined by 'and'. A wrong answer 'one' shows the student counts sentences, not subject-verb pairs.

questions.q: A phrase is a word-group with no ______ pair ('in the morning').
Fill in the blank: A ______ is a group of words with its own subject and verb.
Fill in the blank: The subject-verb test decides everything: 'after the match ended' — subject 'match', verb 'ended' → ______. 'after the match' — no verb → phrase.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student separates phrases from clauses and independent from dependent clauses, and explains why 'when the bell rang' alone is incomplete.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The subject-verb test decides ______: 'after the match ended' — subject 'match', verb 'ended' → clause. 'after the match' — no verb → phrase.
